summary: The article provides largely accurate information regarding Professional Tax in India, its deduction, and state-specific rules, citing relevant sections of the Income Tax Act and the Constitution.

claims.claim: You can claim the Professional Tax paid as a deduction from your gross salary under Section 16(iii) of the Income Tax Act.
claims.note: Section 16(iii) of the Income Tax Act allows for the deduction of professional tax paid from salary income.

claims.claim: Professional Tax is a direct tax levied by state governments under Article 276 of the Constitution of India.
claims.note: Article 276 of the Constitution of India grants state governments the power to levy taxes on professions, trades, callings, and employments.

claims.claim: The maximum amount of Professional Tax that can be levied on an individual in a financial year is capped at ₹2,500, as per the Income Tax Act, 1961.
claims.note: The maximum professional tax that can be levied is ₹2,500 per annum, as per Article 276(2) of the Constitution of India, which is referenced in the Income Tax Act.

claims.claim: States like Delhi or Haryana won't pay it at all, as these states do not levy this tax.
claims.note: Several sources confirm that Delhi and Haryana are among the states that do not levy professional tax.

claims.claim: For self-employed professionals or business owners, the Professional Tax paid is treated as a business expense. This means it can be deducted from your gross professional or business income before calculating your taxable profit. This deduction is allowed under Section 37(1) of the Income Tax Act, which permits the deduction of any expenditure (not being capital expenditure or personal expenses of the assessee) laid out or expended wholly and exclusively for the purposes of the business or profession.
claims.note: Section 37(1) of the Income Tax Act allows for the deduction of expenses incurred wholly and exclusively for business or professional purposes, provided they are not capital or personal expenses. Professional tax paid by self-employed individuals is considered a business expense.
